lines: Morgan Kim
+1 (555) 010-8173 | morgan.kim@example.com | example.com/code/mkim
EDUCATION
Clearwater Institute of Technology | B.S. in Electrical Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2017 - May 2021
EXPERIENCE
Clearwater Sensors | Hardware Test Engineer | Metro City, USA | Apr 2022 - Feb 2023
- Automated end-of-line tests for a humidity sensor, cutting test time per unit from 90 to 25 seconds across 20,000 units a month.
- Traced a batch of early field failures to a solder-paste change; the findings updated the reflow profile and cut returns from 2.1% to 0.4%.
- Wrote the calibration procedure for the sensor line, cutting calibration drift complaints from 15 to 2 a quarter.
- Designed a test fixture that checked 8 boards at once, raising station throughput from 40 to 150 boards an hour.
Voltline Robotics | Embedded Software Engineer | Metro City, USA | Mar 2023 - Jun 2025
- Improved update speed by 60% by compressing firmware images and resuming interrupted downloads.
- Wrote a hardware-in-the-loop test rig that ran 400 motor-control tests on every firmware build.
- Added a crash logger that saved the last 2 seconds of sensor data to flash, which found the root cause of 5 field failures.
- Sampled the motor's 5 kHz vibration signal at 8 kHz so the fault detector could capture it without aliasing.
- Fixed a race condition on the counter shared by the interrupt handler and the main loop by declaring the counter volatile.
- Rewrote the motor-controller firmware for a warehouse robot fleet of 300 units, cutting control-loop jitter from 120 to 15 microseconds and field motor faults by 60%.
PROJECTS
Low-Power Weather Station | Independent Project | C, STM32 | Jan 2025 - Present
- Engineered a next-generation, innovation-driven IoT solution that redefines sustainable environmental sensing.
- Cut average current from 4.2 mA to 0.9 mA by sleeping between readings and batching radio transmissions.
- Published the schematics and firmware openly, and a local school built two stations from them.
Formula Student Electric Car | Electronics Lead, Team of 12 | C | Sep 2019 - May 2021
- Worked on firmware and testing for the robot fleet's motor controllers.
- The CAN-bus firmware for the dashboard was written and tested against the motor controller before each race.
- Rewrote motor-control firmware for a fleet of about 300 robots, cutting control-loop jitter eightfold and motor faults by more than half.
SKILLS
Tools: C, C++, STM32, oscilloscopes
Methods: firmware, hardware-in-the-loop testing, CAN, low-power design

items.says: Experience is not ordered newest-first: Clearwater Sensors appears above Voltline Robotics.
items.because: The older hardware-test role delays the stronger introduction to the more recent embedded-software work.

items.says: Education appears before the more recent Experience and Projects entries.
items.because: Its placement postpones the stronger evidence from the 2023–2025 embedded role.

items.says: No study or work is listed for the 10 months between the degree and the first role.
“Automated end-of-line tests” does not identify the testing step automated.
The solder-paste conclusion is given without showing the diagnostic work.
“The findings updated the reflow profile” makes the findings appear to perform the update.
“Wrote the calibration procedure” does not say what changed about calibration.
“Update speed by 60%” does not identify the metric that improved.
“By 60% by compressing” repeats “by” and slows the sentence.
Running 400 tests reports activity but not its effect.
“Wrote a hardware-in-the-loop test rig” leaves unclear whether you built the rig or only wrote its software.
The wording attributes the investigation to the crash logger rather than clarifying its role.
An 8 kHz sampling rate cannot capture a 5 kHz vibration signal without aliasing.
items.because: Its Nyquist frequency is 4 kHz, so a 5 kHz component aliases to 3 kHz under ordinary sampling.

items.says: “So the fault detector could capture it” describes a purpose, not an observed detection result.
Declaring the shared counter volatile does not, by itself, fix a race condition.
items.because: Volatile does not make accesses atomic or synchronize the interrupt handler with the main loop.

items.says: “Fixed a race condition” does not identify the failure or incorrect behavior addressed.
The shared-counter phrasing repeats “the counter” and stacks two “by” phrases.
items.because: The repetition makes the technical explanation more cumbersome.

items.says: The 300-unit fleet rewrite and its results are also attributed to the earlier Formula Student project.
items.because: The project’s fleet size, jitter reduction and fault reduction match this role’s achievement.

items.says: The fleet-rewrite result is buried at the end of the Voltline entry.
items.because: Its scale and results make it the entry’s strongest result.

items.says: “Rewrote the motor-controller firmware” does not identify the technical change behind the lower jitter.
“Next-generation, innovation-driven IoT solution” is promotional wording that does not identify what was built.
items.because: The broad labels do not show which part of the station demonstrates engineering skill.

items.says: “Redefines sustainable environmental sensing” asserts an effect without saying what changed.
The measured current reduction is not the project’s opening bullet.
items.because: It immediately shows both a result and how it was achieved.

items.says: “Openly” adds little to “Published” without a specific licensing meaning.
The Formula Student entry incorrectly attributes robot-fleet motor-controller work to the student project.
items.because: The car project ended in 2021, while the résumé places robot-fleet work in the later Voltline role.

items.says: “Worked on firmware and testing” does not say what was changed or tested.
items.because: A reader cannot tell what contribution or outcome to credit to you.

items.says: “Tested against the motor controller” does not identify what the dashboard test verified.
“Before each race” gives the test schedule but not its outcome.
“Was written and tested” hides whether you personally did the dashboard CAN work.
The dashboard CAN bullet is not the opening bullet of the car project.
items.because: It belongs under the electric-car heading and would establish the project’s subject first.

items.says: The rewrite for a fleet of about 300 robots is incorrectly presented as Formula Student work.
items.because: The résumé assigns matching fleet, jitter and fault results to the later Voltline role.

items.says: “Rewrote motor-control firmware” does not explain what changed in the control implementation.
items.because: The improvements are not connected to a technical decision, making the work behind them hard to assess.
